summary: Team Stellar's project identifies Earth locations that resemble the environmental conditions of the Moon and Mars, helping researchers prepare for future space exploration. We shortlisted 12 analog sites across the world, including Lonar Crater and Ladakh in India, and compared them using six criteria: geology, regolith, temperature, illumination, water resources, and operational isolation. We propose a data-driven similarity scoring method using NASA and ESA datasets to identify suitable locations for testing technologies and preparing for future lunar and Martian missions. Our work provides a structured foundation for selecting Earth analog sites.
details:
Our project focuses on identifying suitable Earth analog locations for future permanent Moon bases and Mars exploration. It begins by identifying important lunar and Martian regions and selecting 12 potential Earth analog sites across different geographical environments.

Each site is evaluated using six criteria: geology and terrain, regolith and dust, temperature and climate, light and illumination, water and resources, and isolation and operations.

The proposed methodology uses open planetary and Earth observation resources from NASA and ESA. A weighted similarity index is designed to compare the selected locations and identify the closest environmental matches.

The project includes a geographic map prototype showing the 12 shortlisted locations and their Moon/Mars analog categories. The proposed next stage is to develop an interactive map with location profiles, filtering options and evidence-based similarity scores.

The project aims to support researchers, engineers and students in selecting suitable environments for testing technologies and preparing for future lunar and Martian missions.
